summary: Audit mode changes nothing in AWS. It describes what deny mode would refuse, so you can tag every agent before turning the gate on.

would_deny.unless: the calling principal carries the authsec:agent tag (a role tag, an IAM user tag, or a session tag set by an administrator)
tag_protection: setting authsec:agent as a session tag (sts:TagSession, sts:AssumeRole* with tags)
setting authsec:agent on a role or user (iam:TagRole, iam:TagUser, iam:CreateRole, iam:CreateUser)
all refused except for the administrator principals you name (aws:PrincipalArn)

affected.scp: Every principal in the targeted accounts that calls one of the actions above without the tag, except in the management account and service-linked roles (SCPs do not apply there).
affected.policy: Only the roles you attach the AuthSec policy to, when they call one of the actions above without the tag.

report: In AuthSec, open the AI workloads of this account: every identity listed there was seen calling a model (CloudTrail).
Each identity without the authsec:agent tag is one deny mode would refuse. For a shared role, every workload on it is refused together.

Model calls through the agents runtime, bedrock-mantle and AgentCore appear only with the event stream and its data events turned on; without them, an untagged caller of those endpoints is not in the list and would still be refused.
After deny mode is on, refused calls appear in AuthSec as refused model calls with the identity, so anything missed here shows up there.
tagging_guide: Decide which roles are agents. Tag only those: the tag is what lets them call models once the gate is on.
Tag a role: aws iam tag-role --role-name <role> --tags Key=authsec:agent,Value=<agent name>
Tag an IAM user (prefer moving the agent to a role): aws iam tag-user --user-name <user> --tags Key=authsec:agent,Value=<agent name>
Tag with the principals you will name as administrators: deny mode refuses everyone else setting or removing the tag, including pipelines and CloudFormation roles you do not list.
Do not pass authsec:agent as a session tag from an application; set it on the role.
Re-scan in AuthSec and check that no identity you want to keep calling models is still untagged, then deploy the deny template for your form (mode=deny).
